notes: The workbook titled 'Global Health Estimates 2023' covers 2000–2023 and replaces the edition the WHO 2024 report used. Its 2021 values differ a lot from the report's rounded regional figures: Western Pacific 95,882 vs the report's 84,000; Eastern Mediterranean 23,776 vs 35,000; Europe 16,972 vs 15,000; Africa 69,522 vs 66,000; Americas 19,541 vs 17,000; South-East Asia 94,187 vs 83,000; Global 319,879 vs 300,228. So the acceptance point 'whether the 2021 values match the report's rounded figures' has a clear answer: they do not, because this is a later edition with revised data and methods, which the workbook says explicitly. The old rows are not corrected; they stay as the earlier edition's figures. Consequence for toll.json: the core layer's ceiling (300,228, GHE 2021 edition) is below this edition's 2021 and 2023 values; a maintainer should decide whether the core layer moves to the newest edition, keeping both visible. No sums: each regional value is the workbook's own; the Global row is WHO's own total. Crude rates in notes are deaths divided by the sheet's own population, shown so readers can compare with the report's rates, and are not rows.
